name: Montserrat

tax.name: Montserrat Customs and Revenue Service (Inland Revenue)

legalStatuses.label: Sole trader (registered business)
legalStatuses.plain: You run the business as an individual under your own name or a business name. You and the business are the same person for tax. Usually the simplest way to start.
legalStatuses.feeNote: The Financial Services Commission registers the business name and quotes the current fee. Businesses registered under the Micro and Small Business Act can get up to five years of income-tax exemption.

legalStatuses.label: Limited company
legalStatuses.plain: The company is its own legal person, separate from you. It costs more to set up and has more paperwork, but it can limit your personal risk.
legalStatuses.feeNote: A company costs more to set up than a sole trader business. The Financial Services Commission quotes the current fees.

launchSteps.label: Choose your business name and check that it is free
launchSteps.plain: Search the name at the Financial Services Commission first.

launchSteps.label: Register the business name, or incorporate the company, with the Financial Services Commission
launchSteps.plain: A sole trader registers the business name. A company is incorporated.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Inland Revenue and get your tax code
launchSteps.plain: Self-employed people pay provisional income tax in three equal instalments.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Social Security Fund
launchSteps.plain: Self-employed people choose a weekly income band and pay a percentage of it.

launchSteps.label: Ask about the Micro and Small Business incentives
launchSteps.plain: A qualifying micro or small business can get up to five years of income-tax exemption and stamp-duty relief.

launchSteps.label: Open a separate bank account for the business
launchSteps.plain: Keeping business money apart from household money makes your numbers clearer and your taxes easier to pay.

launchSteps.label: Register as an employer and prepare monthly payments
launchSteps.plain: With employees you deduct income tax (PAYE) and Social Security and pay them by the 14th of the following month.

launchSteps.label: Register for VAT
launchSteps.plain: Required when your taxable sales pass EC$300,000 a year.

contributions.label: Social Security
contributions.plain: Social Security gives access to a pension and other benefits. Since January 2026 self-employed people pay 12% of their declared income. It lowers your taxable income.

vat.label: Value Added Tax
vat.registerNote: Register once your taxable sales pass this level in a year.
vat.filingNote: Your filing period is set when you register.

calendar.monthlyText: Self-employed people pay provisional income tax in three equal instalments: the Inland Revenue gives you the dates when you register.
calendar.annualTextPersonal: File your annual income tax return.
calendar.payrollText: Every month: pay income tax (PAYE) and Social Security for the previous month, by the 14th.
calendar.vatText: If you are registered for VAT: file your return for each period.

notes: A micro or small business registered under the Micro and Small Business Act can get up to five years of income-tax exemption and stamp-duty relief: ask when you register.

sources.label: Montserrat Income and Corporation Tax (Amendment) Act 2024
